newsitem.title: USA: U.S. trucking group to sue EPA over clean air plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. trucking group to sue EPA over clean air plan.

text.p: The American Trucking Association said Friday it will file a lawsuit challenging the Environmental Protection Agency's plan to set tight new limits on smog and soot.

The group was the first to threaten a lawsuit, although several industries are battling the new air quality standards for smog-forming ozone and fine particles that lodge in the lungs that President Bill Clinton endorsed this week.

The trucking group said that EPA had "failed to live up to legal provisions of the Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Fairness Act, which requires the agency to cnosider how the standards will impact small business."
It added that the rules were based on "inadequate science," an argument made by industry groups and several lawmakers over the last few months.

"These rules will be monumentally costly to small businesses and consumers," the group said, adding that it "cannot stand for regulations that are of questionable merit, with considerable uncertainty, and with a very high price tag for all involved."

Democrats and Republicans from industrial states plan to launch a legislative assault on the new standards which Environmental Protection Agency administrator Carol Browner said were needed to protect millions of children and prevent 15,000 premature deaths each year from lung ailments.
